notes: Run with the skill and again without it, in fresh sessions, and compare. Runs must not write to Linear: 'proposes without writing' is an assertion in every case, not a side effect to tolerate.

evals.prompt: we should do something about onboarding, it's not great. can you get that into Linear?
evals.expected_output: No object created. Either a small number of clarifying questions, or one proposed outcome offered for confirmation with its unknowns named.
assertions: Nothing is written to Linear
The response does not invent a scope, a target date, an owner, or a priority
It either asks what specifically is wrong with onboarding or proposes a single outcome and labels it as a proposal
If a title is proposed, it names an outcome rather than the topic 'onboarding'

evals.prompt: File a bug: users with two identity providers get a blank page after the SSO redirect, the API returns 400. Two enterprise tenants hit it in production yesterday. Doesn't happen with one provider. Error is AuthError: ambiguous provider binding.
evals.expected_output: A previewed issue with a declarative title naming the wrong behaviour, a body of roughly four lines covering observed, expected, where it was seen, and the error line, and no invented priority or assignee.
assertions: The title is declarative and names the observed failure, not a fix
The title contains no type prefix, priority, or component tag
The body states what was observed and what was expected
Yesterday is converted to an absolute date, or the response says the date was not established
Priority and assignee are left unset, or the response says explicitly why they were set
The body has no empty headings and no section that restates the title
A preview is shown and nothing is written to Linear without approval

evals.prompt: Here's a Linear issue description I wrote. Can you clean it up? [1,200 words containing file paths, a SQL snippet, a migration plan, a test plan, and a section on alternatives considered, describing a fix to search so it includes issues from archived projects]
evals.expected_output: A rewritten description of roughly 100 to 150 words covering the observable problem and the constraint, with everything removed relocated explicitly rather than dropped.
assertions: The rewritten description states the observable problem before any implementation detail
SQL, the test plan, and the migration plan are removed from the Linear description
The response says where each removed piece should go, naming a pull request, a GitHub issue, an ADR, or a comment
Nothing factual in the original is silently discarded
The response does not write the change to Linear without approval

evals.prompt: We keep going back and forth on whether the database schema is defined by Drizzle or by the hardcoded SQL constant. Can you create a Linear issue to sort this out?
evals.expected_output: An issue whose deliverable is an accepted ADR, with the analysis routed to the record rather than into the issue body.
assertions: The response identifies this as an architectural decision that belongs in an ADR
It proposes a Linear issue whose outcome is an accepted decision record, rather than putting the analysis in the issue
It references the writing-adrs skill or docs/adr rather than drafting the decision itself
It does not assert which option is correct as though it were decided

evals.prompt: Create a project in Linear for the work to reduce failed SSO logins for enterprise customers. Aim for end of Q3.
evals.expected_output: A previewed project with a one-sentence summary, a short description covering why, success, and scope, a target date at quarter resolution, and unknowns named rather than filled.
assertions: A project summary of one sentence is proposed, and it is distinct from the description
The description does not contain project status
The target date uses quarter resolution rather than an invented specific day
No baseline or target metric is stated as fact unless the user supplied one
Any milestones proposed are named as states that can become true, not as teams, layers, or phase numbers
The lead is left unset unless the user named one

evals.prompt: Can you add the Postgres connection pooling work to Linear? It's blocking the migration and Dana said it should be done by the 20th.
evals.expected_output: A previewed issue that carries the stated blocker and date, sets a blocked-by relation only if the blocking object can be identified, and asks rather than guessing what it cannot resolve.
assertions: The date from the user is recorded, and the year is either resolved from context or queried rather than assumed silently
A blocking relationship is proposed only against an object that exists, otherwise the response says which object it could not find
Dana is not assigned as owner merely because she was mentioned
The title names the outcome rather than 'Postgres work'
Unknowns are listed explicitly in the preview

evals.prompt: Can you add a Linear issue for renaming the internal config key AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS to RUN_TIMEOUT_MS? It's used in three places.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation that this needs no Linear object, with the pull request offered as the record, and compliance if the user still wants it tracked.
assertions: The response recommends creating no Linear object, or explicitly raises that option first
It gives the reason: the change is small, self-contained, and has no consequence anyone would ask about later
It offers the pull request as the place the change is recorded
It does not refuse outright, and would proceed if the user insisted

evals.prompt: Please improve this Linear issue. Title: 'Accept skill frontmatter that closes with more than three dashes'. Description: 'Skill files whose frontmatter closes with a longer dash run are rejected as malformed, so the skill silently does not load. Accept the longer fence, and cover the malformed case in a test.'
evals.expected_output: A statement that the issue is already accurate, current, and readable, and no rewrite.
assertions: The response makes no substantive change to the title or description
It says explicitly that the object is fine as it stands
It does not add headings, acceptance criteria, or a context section
It does not propose a stylistic rephrasing as though it were an improvement

evals.prompt: File an issue: the onboarding email is landing in spam. Dana thinks it probably affects around 30% of new signups but we haven't measured it.
evals.expected_output: An issue that keeps the 30% figure with its status as an unmeasured estimate and its attribution, rather than dropping it or stating it as fact.
assertions: The 30% figure is preserved rather than dropped
It is marked as an estimate and attributed to Dana, not written as a measured fact
The response does not add a fabricated measurement method or source
The title states the observed problem rather than the estimated impact

evals.prompt: Create an issue to replace our custom Redis lock implementation with the standard locking abstraction.
evals.expected_output: An issue whose title names the technical change, without an invented user-facing benefit.
assertions: The title names the replacement itself rather than a user outcome
No user-facing or reliability benefit is asserted unless the user supplied evidence for it
If a motivation is included, it is attributed or marked as inferred
The issue is not converted into a project
